UNH.rationale: UNH presents a mixed but slightly positive picture. On fundamentals, the company is a dominant healthcare franchise with strong scale ($111.7B quarterly revenue, largest US health insurer), solid cash generation ($8.91B operating cash flow in Q1 2026), and balance balance sheet (equity $103.9B, debt-to-equity ~2.0x). However, trajectory is mediocre: YoY revenue growth of only +2.0%, net income essentially flat (+0.1% YoY), and margins have compressed significantly (net margin 2.8% vs 5.6% a year ago, operating margin 4.2%). The company is actively cutting ~1.3M Medicare Advantage members to protect profitability, which is a defensive move rather than growth-oriented. On valuation, the stock has re-rated sharply: P/E of 28.2x is near the top of its 365-day range (9.5-28.5) and well above the ~12-16x range that prevailed for most of the past year. P/B of 3.47x is also at the top of its range (2.2-3.5). This re-rating appears driven by Q1 earnings beat ($7.23 adjusted EPS vs $6.61 consensus) and raised FY2026 guidance to >$18.25 adjusted EPS, plus favorable Medicare Advantage rate announcements. The stock has surged +37.3% in the past quarter. While the earnings beat and guidance raise are genuine positives, the stock now trades at a significant premium to its recent history, and the fundamental trajectory (flat earnings, margin compression, membership cuts) does not clearly justify this multiple expansion. Near-term catalysts are limited: the next earnings report is Aug 4, and the Medicare Advantage rate news is already priced in. Berkshire Hathaway's full exit from UNH in Q1 2026 is a sentiment headwind. Regulatory risks (DOJ investigations, PBM scrutiny, mental health coverage practices) remain meaningful overhangs. The score reflects a quality franchise at an elevated valuation with modest near-term upside from current levels.
